lane: datum-offset lane — Lake Lahontan shorelines as a strain gauge
hypothesis: The Lahontan highstand shoreline is a near-level datum (~15 ka); a fault that cuts it produces an abrupt step or a lateral deflection that is measurable in the DEM and locatable where no catalogue fault is mapped.
mechanism: fit a smooth isobase to the highstand band, take the datum residual zeta = z - isobase, trace its zero contour, flag vertical steps and heading changes along each trace, seed a dot train at every flag, extend it along the local DEM-ridge direction, thin to 282.8 m, prune 3 px off the catalogue
non_fault_process_that_could_mimic_it: Post-pluvial isostatic rebound and northward tilting tilt the datum by ~20 m across the basin (Adams, Wesnousky & Bills 1999; Adams et al. 2008). A fitted quadratic absorbs part of that tilt into its curvature terms, so a rebound gradient can masquerade as a step. Wave-cut terrace/berm constructional relief (<2.6 m within an embayment, Adams & Wesnousky 1998) is a second mimic at the same amplitude as the flagged steps.
